model.title: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act of 2025

summary.lead: Official summary (Congressional Research Service, Introduced in House):

blocks.text: Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act of 2025
This bill takes approximately 204.14 acres of specified lands in El Dorado County, California, into trust for the benefit of the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians.

The bill revokes a specified public land order and administratively transfers the land from the Forest Service to the Department of the Interior. (In the public land order, the land was designated for use by the Forest Service as an experiment station.)

The bill directs Interior to take the following lands into trust for the benefit of the tribe: (1) approximately 85.3 acres of federal land managed by Interior's Bureau of Land Management (which includes the land transferred from the Forest Service), and (2) approximately 118.84 acres of fee land held by the tribe. These combined lands, approximately 204.14 acres, shall be part of the tribe's reservation. Further, the bill prohibits gaming on the land taken into trust.
The Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians Land Transfer Act of 2025 would place about 204.14 acres of land in El Dorado County, California, into trust for the Shingle Springs Band of Miwok Indians.

To make this possible, the bill cancels a specified public land order and moves the land from the Forest Service to the Department of the Interior. That public land order had set the land aside for use by the Forest Service as an experiment station.

The bill directs the Department of the Interior to take two groups of land into trust for the tribe. The first is about 85.3 acres of federal land managed by the Bureau of Land Management, which includes the land moved over from the Forest Service. The second is about 118.84 acres of land the tribe already holds in fee. Together these add up to about 204.14 acres, and they will become part of the tribe's reservation. The bill also bans gaming on the land placed in trust.
